event: The voice: it's me; you can close your eyes, nothing here needs them.
Nothing is required tonight; the day is over, and the unfinished will keep until morning.
The story asks nothing; losing it is winning, and that is the whole game tonight.
You walk a soft dirt road at dusk, gently downhill, each step easier than the last.
Ahead is only a waystation by a lake, the water going violet as the day lets go.
Small and warm-windowed, it has been expecting you all day.
Travelers here are safe: the road's oldest rule, never once broken.
At the gate a soft low chime sounds: "Welcome, traveler. Rest, level one."

changes.note: The System marks Rest at level one as Alan reaches the gate

event: The System here only notices each small kindness you do yourself, and writes it down.
You push the gate open; it swings easy on oiled hinges.
The violet-eyed keeper meets you at the door and asks you not a single question.
She steps aside and lets you in where it's warm.
A fire hums orange, bread waits on the hearthstone, a chair is built for your tiredness.
You hang your cloak on the peg by the door.
Chime: "Letting go, level one."

changes.note: Hanging up his cloak marks Letting go at level one

event: Here setting things down counts as progress; the numbers rise when you stop carrying.
You sit, and the chair takes your whole weight.
Your shoulders come down half an inch without being told.
Chime: "Rest, level two."

changes.note: Sitting in the chair raises Rest to level two

event: The keeper brings you tea; you watch the steam rise and lean.
It will stay warm as long as you need; you needn't drink it yet.
You eat the dense, honest, slightly sweet bread slowly.
Behind you the keeper moves like water, humming two notes at a time.
You will never quite catch the tune, and you're not supposed to.
Chime: "Ease, level one."

changes.note: Tea and bread by the fire mark Ease at level one

event: The numbers grow quieter; the System lowers its voice as you settle.
Through the window the lake has gone fully violet, flat and still.
The last birds have made their arrangements for the night.
A moth bumps softly at the lantern glass, patient and unhurried.
The keeper shows you to your room up shallow stairs.
The banister is smooth from a hundred years of tired hands.
The room is small the way good rooms are; the deep bed takes up most of it.
The heavy blankets press you kindly into the mattress: done now. Done.
You lie down.
Chime, softer now, almost underwater: "Rest, level three."

changes.note: Lying down in the deep bed raises Rest to level three

event: Rest three lets you hear the lake: water against the dock posts. Tap.
It has said the same thing every night; you needn't listen, only let it be there.
Your feet are warm now.
Your hands have nothing to hold; they've earned that.
Below, the keeper banks the fire; the light under your door fades from orange to nothing.
She will be there in the morning, and so will the waystation.
Tonight the road is closed on purpose; the gate is latched, opening only from inside.
Chime, so quiet now: "Letting go, level two."

changes.note: Lying still as the house goes dark raises Letting go to level two

event: The numbers will keep counting for you while you sleep.
The place's secret: you gain the most levels in the hours you remember nothing.
All night the System sits by your bed like a small patient lamp, marking things down.
Breath slower, shoulders loose, day released: level, level.
By morning you'll be richer and won't know why.
The water touches the dock post. Tap.
The moth has settled somewhere, wings folded.
The keeper's two-note tune goes on under the floor, or it's the house settling.
You're warm and safe in the bed by the violet lake; nothing is coming, nothing owed.
The lake goes on saying its one soft thing. Tap.
"Sleep now. I've got the lamp."
